skill.name: prompt-architect
skill.description: A structured prompt engineering skill for analyzing, creating, and refining prompts for AI language models.
skill.summary: Analyze and improve prompts with clear structure, evidence-based techniques, and anti-pattern checks.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: All twelve static detections are false positives caused by prose examples and Markdown delimiters. No evidence found of command execution, network reconnaissance, system reconnaissance, prompt injection, or data-exfiltration intent in the reviewed files.

static_findings.snippet: - Good: "Output must be valid JSON matching this schema: {...}"
- Good: "Extract all emails. Return empty array if none found. Skip invalid format emails."
- Bad: Creative writing with rigid step-by-step constraints
To avoid anti-patterns from the start:
- Triple backticks for code or data: ```data here```
- Use negative examples to illustrate what to avoid
- "Extract email addresses from the text" (what if there are none? multiple formats? invalid ones?)
- Ask AI to show its thinking process

content.value_statement: Reusable AI prompts often fail because goals, context, and output requirements are unclear. This skill helps you analyze, restructure, and improve prompts with systematic checks.
actual_capabilities: Reviews prompts for clarity, structure, context, and output requirements.
Identifies common prompt anti-patterns such as vague goals, contradictions, and missing edge cases.
Suggests evidence-based techniques including few-shot examples, self-consistency checks, and plan-and-solve structure.
Adapts prompt guidance for analytical, coding, creative writing, transformation, and question-answering tasks.
Helps convert weak prompts into reusable templates for teams or repeated workflows.
limitations: It provides prompt design guidance, not guaranteed model performance.
It does not test prompts against live model outputs unless the user provides results.
It cannot validate facts, citations, or domain claims without source material.
It may need user context to tailor prompts for specialized industries or policies.

use_cases.title: Improve Team Prompt Templates
use_cases.description: Convert inconsistent team prompts into clearer reusable templates with explicit context, constraints, and output expectations.

use_cases.title: Design Reliable Coding Prompts
use_cases.description: Create prompts that specify language, version, requirements, error handling, and expected behavior for code generation tasks.

use_cases.title: Teach Prompt Engineering Basics
use_cases.description: Use the framework to explain why prompt changes improve clarity, reliability, and maintainability.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Simple Prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this prompt for clarity and missing context. Explain the main weaknesses, then provide a revised version that keeps the original goal.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Reusable Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this task into a reusable prompt template. Include placeholders, required context, output format, edge cases, and quality checks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Prompt Library
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these prompts as a library. Group recurring issues, identify duplicated patterns, recommend standard sections, and prioritize fixes by impact.

prompt_templates.title: Design a High-Stakes Workflow Prompt
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt architecture for complex work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a prompt for this high-stakes workflow. Include planning, execution, verification, uncertainty handling, and clear limits on what the model should not assume.

output_examples.input: A user asks to improve a prompt that says, Analyze this customer feedback.
output_examples.output: The result explains that the prompt lacks goal, audience, categories, and output format. It rewrites the prompt to request themes, sentiment, evidence, and next actions.

output_examples.input: A team wants a repeatable prompt for bug report triage.
output_examples.output: The result defines required inputs, severity criteria, edge-case handling, and a concise triage format for repeated engineering use.

output_examples.input: A prompt library produces inconsistent summaries across models.
output_examples.output: The result identifies missing length rules, weak examples, and unclear success criteria. It recommends shared template sections and model-specific testing.

best_practices: State the task, audience, constraints, and desired output before adding examples.
Use examples to clarify expected behavior, especially for repeated or team workflows.
Test refined prompts with edge cases and revise based on observed failures.
anti_patterns: Asking for broad analysis without defining purpose, scope, or success criteria.
Adding many nested rules before the core task is clear.
Assuming the model knows private standards, team formats, or missing background.

faq.question: What does Prompt Architect help me do?
faq.answer: It helps you analyze, create, and refine prompts for AI systems using structured prompt engineering methods.

faq.question: Can it create prompts for Claude and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports prompt design for Claude, Codex, Claude Code, ChatGPT, and other language models.

faq.question: Does it run code or call external services?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation-based and provides prompt engineering guidance inside the assistant workflow.

faq.question: Is it useful for nontechnical users?
faq.answer: Yes. The framework uses plain prompt design principles that apply to writing, research, operations, and education tasks.

faq.question: How should I provide context?
faq.answer: Share the current prompt, the expected audience, the desired output, and examples of failures or good results.

faq.question: Does it guarantee better AI answers?
faq.answer: No. It improves prompt quality, but results still depend on the model, input quality, and task difficulty.
